name: Common arterial trunk with pulmonary dominance and interrupted aortic arch
aliases: Truncus arteriosus with pulmonary dominance and interrupted aortic arch
Pulmonary dominant common arterial trunk with interrupted aortic arch

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and cardiac MRI diagnostic criteria for common arterial trunk with interrupted aortic arch

criteria.description: Presence of a single arterial trunk arising from the heart supplying systemic, pulmonary, and coronary circulations
Pulmonary artery component predominates in the common trunk anatomy
Complete discontinuity of the aortic arch confirmed by imaging
Presence of a large ventricular septal defect beneath the common arterial trunk

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a single arterial trunk with pulmonary dominance combined with interrupted aortic arch on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on echocardiography and cardiac MRI or CT angiography.

pathognomonic.notes: Harsh systolic murmur heard on auscultation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate

common.notes: Increased work of breathing due to pulmonary overcirculation
Elevated heart rate secondary to heart failure

occasional.notes: Elevated pulmonary artery pressures on catheterization
Poor feeding due to fatigue and respiratory distress

searchTerms: nerve issues from lack of oxygen

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to low cardiac output
rare.notes: Acute kidney injury in severe cases
searchTerms: kidney problems from poor heart pumping
reduced kidney function due to low blood flow
kidney damage from weak heart output

rare.notes: Infective endocarditis on the common trunk or valves

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating single arterial trunk with pulmonary dominance
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming interrupted aortic arch
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings

distinguishingFeatures: Aortic dominance of the common trunk rather than pulmonary dominance
Presence of four characteristic defects including overriding aorta and right ventricular outflow obstruction

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
